### saying.util.clog(condition, \*args, log_func=<built-in function print>, \*\*kwargs)

Conditional log

```pycon
>>> clog(False, "logging this")
>>> clog(True, "logging this")
logging this
```

### saying.util.extract_sql_data(text, \*, bytes_decoder=<method 'decode' of 'bytes' objects>)

Extracts data from sql dump text: one `[field, ...]` list per row of each
`INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...),(...);` statement.

Rows are recognised even when the `),(` separators are pretty-printed
across lines (as MySQL dumps often are):

```pycon
>>> text = '''
... -- MySQL dump 10.13  ...
... ...
... INSERT INTO `quotes` (col1,col2,col3) VALUES
... (1,'One', 1.0),
... (2,'Two', 2.0),
... (3,'Three', 3.0);
... '''
>>> extract_sql_data(text)
[['1', "'One'", '1.0'], ['2', "'Two'", '2.0'], ['3', "'Three'", '3.0']]
```

### saying.util.hash_text(text)

Return a hash of the text, ignoring punctuation and capitalization.

```pycon
>>> hash_text('Hello, world!') == hash_text('hello world')
True
>>> hash_text('Hello, world!')
'5eb63bbbe01eeed093cb22bb8f5acdc3'
```

# saying.wikimedia

Get quotes data etc.

### Functions

| [`download_and_process_wiki_data`](_autosummary/saying.wikimedia.html.md#saying.wikimedia.download_and_process_wiki_data)([languages, ...])   | Downloads and processes quotation data from wikimedia and dbpedia.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`parse_wikimedia_xml`](_autosummary/saying.wikimedia.html.md#saying.wikimedia.parse_wikimedia_xml)(file_path)                     | Parse (author, quote_text) pairs from xml file.                      |

### saying.wikimedia.download_and_process_wiki_data(languages='en', data_dir='/home/runner/.config/saying/wikimedia', , date='20231201', datedbpedia2='2022.12.01', verbose=True)

Downloads and processes quotation data from wikimedia and dbpedia.

If you have trouble with it, try running again, and if problems persist, download
the needed resources manually and place them in the data_dir.

You’ll find them here: [https://dumps.wikimedia.org/enwikiquote/](https://dumps.wikimedia.org/enwikiquote/)

### saying.wikimedia.parse_wikimedia_xml(file_path)

Parse (author, quote_text) pairs from xml file.
: The xml file is assumped to be one that has been downloaded from wikimedia
  ([https://dumps.wikimedia.org/enwikiquote/](https://dumps.wikimedia.org/enwikiquote/)).
  For example, using the `download_and_process_wiki_data` function.

Note the relative filepath has, at the time of writing this, the format
`"{language}/pages.xml"` (e.g. `"en/pages.xml"`)
